pr_body:
Closes #40603

```c#
namespace System
{
    partial class Uri
    {
        public static string EscapeDataString(ReadOnlySpan<char> charsToEscape);
        public static bool TryEscapeDataString(ReadOnlySpan<char> charsToEscape, Span<char> destination, out int charsWritten);

        public static string UnescapeDataString(ReadOnlySpan<char> charsToUnescape);
        public static bool TryUnescapeDataString(ReadOnlySpan<char> charsToUnescape, Span<char> destination, out int charsWritten);
    }
}
```

The test coverage for these was not great, so I added a bunch more combinations. I also moved similar test cases from `System.Runtime.Tests` into the Uri project.

I updated `FormUrlEncodedContent` to also use these, so it's now allocating a lot less. For a random usage I pulled from [eShopOnWeb tests](https://github.com/dotnet-architecture/eShopOnWeb/blob/2fa4a3d3368381818c6191122d037c6a70b302f5/tests/FunctionalTests/Web/Controllers/AccountControllerSignIn.cs#L63-L69):
| Method             | Toolchain  | Mean     | Error   | Ratio | Allocated | Alloc Ratio |
|------------------- |----------- |---------:|--------:|------:|----------:|------------:|
| EShopOnWebLogin    | main       | 513.7 ns | 1.69 ns |  1.00 |    2080 B |        1.00 |
| EShopOnWebLogin    | pr         | 291.3 ns | 1.47 ns |  0.57 |     592 B |        0.28 |

Looking at something like YARP's [`EncodePath`](https://github.com/microsoft/reverse-proxy/blob/379671ef2afd01e55168929c33c6b5cbcd0b06b0/src/ReverseProxy/Forwarder/RequestUtilities.cs#L132) helper with ASP.NET Core's [test paths](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/14868cc8741fda987431003ea3b06ac01e7fc3f1/src/Http/Http.Abstractions/perf/Microbenchmarks/PathStringBenchmark.cs#L10-L12), the difference is
| Method | Scenario             | Mean      | Error    | Ratio | Allocated | Alloc Ratio |
|------- |--------------------- |----------:|---------:|------:|----------:|------------:|
| Old    | LongTestPath         |  95.51 ns | 0.702 ns |  1.00 |     400 B |        1.00 |
| New    | LongTestPath         |  70.58 ns | 0.291 ns |  0.74 |     344 B |        0.86 |
|        |                      |           |          |       |           |             |
| Old    | LongT(...)rcent [24] | 337.00 ns | 2.713 ns |  1.00 |     392 B |        1.00 |
| New    | LongT(...)rcent [24] | 198.49 ns | 0.892 ns |  0.59 |     280 B |        0.71 |
|        |                      |           |          |       |           |             |
| Old    | TestPath             |  67.28 ns | 0.439 ns |  1.00 |     112 B |        1.00 |
| New    | TestPath             |  44.98 ns | 0.129 ns |  0.67 |      56 B |        0.50 |

@karelz Do you require anything further from me to get this discussed for moving into ready for review?

I would expect this API to only be used in cases like the one you described above - manually optimizing the concatenation of query string parts.

Given that that would be the only use case, would having `QueryHelper` (#32606) APIs be preferable?
Regardless of the public API, that can be more efficient in the final ToString/Serialize operation than what is reasonably achievable today.

Marked #54828 as a duplicate of this since we'd likely want to match span support for `EscapeDataString` and `UnescapeDataString`.

It looks like there's a bit more community interest here, optimistically moving to 8.0
Sadly, we won't make it in 8.0 due to circumstances. Moving to Future for now.

I've updated the proposal to include both the `string Foo(ROS<char>)` and `bool TryFoo(ROS<char>, Span<char>, out int)` overloads, for both `EscapeDataString` and `UnescapeDataString`.
Also updated the parameter names from `string-` to `chars-`, but we can discuss more in API review.

@dotnet/ncl Marking this one as ready for review, scream if you disagree :)

A few more uses in YARP and ASP.NET Core:
- https://github.com/microsoft/reverse-proxy/blob/379671ef2afd01e55168929c33c6b5cbcd0b06b0/src/ReverseProxy/Forwarder/RequestUtilities.cs#L177
